messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Metoprolol is FDA-approved to treat high blood pressure, angina, heart failure, and heart attack, but the two forms are not approved for the same conditions.
Condition | Metoprolol tartrate (immediate release) | Metoprolol succinate (extended release)
High blood pressure (hypertension) in adults | Yes | Yes
High blood pressure in children 6 years and older | No | Yes
Angina (chest pain) | Yes | Yes
Heart failure | No | Yes
Heart attack (myocardial infarction) | Yes | No
High blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal heart and blood vessel events, mainly strokes and heart attacks. Metoprolol can be used on its own or with other blood pressure medicines. Many people need more than one medicine to reach their blood pressure goal.
Angina. Metoprolol is used for long-term treatment of angina, to reduce how often attacks happen and to help you do more before chest pain starts. It is not used to stop an attack that has already begun.
Triplet: ["Metoprolol", "fda approved to treat", "heart attack"]

The relation 'fda approved to treat' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is approved by the FDA to treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'fda approved in combination with': The subject drug is approved by the FDA for use in combination with the substance or drug specified by the object entity.
B. 'treats': The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
C. 'used in': The subject drug is utilized in the medical procedure or clinical context specified by the object entity.
D. 'fda approval year': The subject drug was approved by the US FDA in the year specified by the object entity.
E. 'used in population': The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.
